unfilled.meaning: Nine fixed conditional rate points and, when original positive-time drainage calibration exists, one extra rate from48golden-section steps in each of eight fixed gaps. Three initial-band points each have two explicit capacity witnesses. Original retained and cumulative-drained calibration bands constrain the same initial inventory; no derived observations are inserted. For a nonzero-width rate interval, endpoint starts move inward by min(width/4,64machine epsilons times maximum absolute rate); nominal and sampled fractions are recorded. These are computational grid/search conventions, not extra measurement uncertainty, a certified enclosure or global optimality proof. Every original calibration band is retained. This is a finite computational proposal family, not a continuous enclosure, probability distribution or identified parameter set.

This is a finite computational proposal family, not a continuous enclosure, probability distribution or identified parameter set.

baseline.meaning: Finite central-value and separately enumerated initially-full and initially-empty boundary proposals, conditional on a uniform isolated receiving footprint. Wet surface pairs with a receiver account, post-dry retained pairs and post-dry cumulative drainage triples with an original storm-end depth are examined. Drainage triples may have unequal time spacing; their derived retained course is never inserted into original observations. The post-dry inverse keeps both monotone capacity branches. Only original calibration values generate parameters; every original surface and receiving calibration band must then pass the maintained forward model. Held-aside values only challenge and never select a prospective measurement. No negative fill time or storage is clipped. No fallback, parameter uncertainty enclosure, complete continuous search, unique physical identification or automatic adoption is claimed.

unfilled.meaning: Nine fixed conditional rate points and, when original positive-time drainage calibration exists, one extra rate from48golden-section steps in each of eight fixed gaps. Three initial-band points each have two explicit capacity witnesses. Original retained and cumulative-drained calibration bands constrain the same initial inventory; no derived observations are inserted. For a nonzero-width rate interval, endpoint starts move inward by min(width/4,64machine epsilons times maximum absolute rate); nominal and sampled fractions are recorded. These are computational grid/search conventions, not extra measurement uncertainty, a certified enclosure or global optimality proof. Every original calibration band is retained. This is a finite computational proposal family, not a continuous enclosure, probability distribution or identified parameter set.

baseline.meaning: Finite central-value and separately enumerated initially-full and initially-empty boundary proposals, conditional on a uniform isolated receiving footprint. Wet surface pairs with a receiver account, post-dry retained pairs and post-dry cumulative drainage triples with an original storm-end depth are examined. Drainage triples may have unequal time spacing; their derived retained course is never inserted into original observations. The post-dry inverse keeps both monotone capacity branches. Only original calibration values generate parameters; every original surface and receiving calibration band must then pass the maintained forward model. Held-aside values only challenge and never select a prospective measurement. No negative fill time or storage is clipped. No fallback, parameter uncertainty enclosure, complete continuous search, unique physical identification or automatic adoption is claimed.

unfilled.meaning: Nine fixed conditional rate points and, when original positive-time drainage calibration exists, one extra rate from48golden-section steps in each of eight fixed gaps. Three initial-band points each have two explicit capacity witnesses. Original retained and cumulative-drained calibration bands constrain the same initial inventory; no derived observations are inserted. For a nonzero-width rate interval, endpoint starts move inward by min(width/4,64machine epsilons times maximum absolute rate); nominal and sampled fractions are recorded. These are computational grid/search conventions, not extra measurement uncertainty, a certified enclosure or global optimality proof. Every original calibration band is retained. This is a finite computational proposal family, not a continuous enclosure, probability distribution or identified parameter set.

Three initial-band points each have two explicit capacity witnesses. Original retained and cumulative-drained calibration bands constrain the same initial inventory; no derived observations are inserted. For a nonzero-width rate interval, endpoint starts move inward by min(width/4,64machine epsilons times maximum absolute rate); nominal and sampled fractions are recorded. These are computational grid/search conventions, not extra measurement uncertainty, a certified enclosure or global optimality proof. Every original calibration band is retained. This is a finite computational proposal family, not a continuous enclosure, probability distribution or identified parameter set.

Wet surface pairs with a receiver account, post-dry retained pairs and post-dry cumulative drainage triples with an original storm-end depth are examined. No fallback, parameter uncertainty enclosure, complete continuous search, unique physical identification or automatic adoption is claimed.

unfilled.meaning: Nine fixed conditional rate points and, when original positive-time drainage calibration exists, one extra rate from48golden-section steps in each of eight fixed gaps. Three initial-band points each have two explicit capacity witnesses. Original retained and cumulative-drained calibration bands constrain the same initial inventory; no derived observations are inserted. For a nonzero-width rate interval, endpoint starts move inward by min(width/4,64machine epsilons times maximum absolute rate); nominal and sampled fractions are recorded. These are computational grid/search conventions, not extra measurement uncertainty, a certified enclosure or global optimality proof. Every original calibration band is retained. This is a finite computational proposal family, not a continuous enclosure, probability distribution or identified parameter set.

unfilled.meaning: Nine fixed conditional rate points and, when original positive-time drainage calibration exists, one extra rate from48golden-section steps in each of eight fixed gaps. Three initial-band points each have two explicit capacity witnesses. Original retained and cumulative-drained calibration bands constrain the same initial inventory; no derived observations are inserted. For a nonzero-width rate interval, endpoint starts move inward by min(width/4,64machine epsilons times maximum absolute rate); nominal and sampled fractions are recorded. These are computational grid/search conventions, not extra measurement uncertainty, a certified enclosure or global optimality proof. Every original calibration band is retained. This is a finite computational proposal family, not a continuous enclosure, probability distribution or identified parameter set.

unfilled.meaning: Nine fixed conditional rate points and, when original positive-time drainage calibration exists, one extra rate from48golden-section steps in each of eight fixed gaps. Three initial-band points each have two explicit capacity witnesses. Original retained and cumulative-drained calibration bands constrain the same initial inventory; no derived observations are inserted. For a nonzero-width rate interval, endpoint starts move inward by min(width/4,64machine epsilons times maximum absolute rate); nominal and sampled fractions are recorded. These are computational grid/search conventions, not extra measurement uncertainty, a certified enclosure or global optimality proof. Every original calibration band is retained. This is a finite computational proposal family, not a continuous enclosure, probability distribution or identified parameter set.
